Now I'm going through the 19 candidates to decide how each should be annotated, starting with the first: "Hereditary deficiency of the fifth component of complement." It reads as a specific disease, hereditary C5 deficiency, so I'm leaning toward SpecificDisease, even though "deficiency" on its own is generic.

Going through the rest of the candidates, I'm treating "C5-deficient" and its abbreviation "C5D" as modifiers on the serum rather than disease mentions in their own right, while the full "hereditary deficiency" phrase repeats as a specific disease. "C5" by itself names the protein, so it doesn't count.

Now I'm going through the remaining candidates. "C5" by itself names the protein, so it's not a disease mention, and the same goes for the organisms Escherichia coli, Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Candida albicans. "C5 deficiency" in the heterozygous family sera refers to the disease state itself, so I'm treating it as a SpecificDisease, while the "C5D" abbreviations stay as modifiers on the serum.

I'm settling on how to cite the guidelines for each candidate, using the organism and modifier rules for the non-disease terms, and I'm treating the complement component C5 as a protein name rather than a disease.

Now I'm settling the citations: organism names go under the rule for not annotating them unless a disease is discussed, and the bare "C5" stays unannotated as a protein name. The JSON still needs to be single-line and valid, so I'm keeping quotes out of the rationales.
